name: Phasor measurement unit
summary: Device that measures voltage and current phasors with precise time stamps so angles can be compared across a network.
description: A phasor measurement unit samples voltages and currents and calculates magnitude and phase angle referenced to an absolute time source, normally GPS. Data from many PMUs can then be compared to see angle differences across a network, oscillations and islanding.

On a single-line diagram the PMU is drawn with its CT and VT inputs and a time input. The symbol does not show reporting rate, the communications path to a data concentrator or the measurement class, which together determine whether the data suits protection, control or monitoring.
readingNotes: Trace CT and VT inputs to the measuring point.
distinction: A PMU reports time-aligned phasors; a phase-angle meter shows a local angle between two inputs.
